summary: WP-004 is a build-verification WP with no source modifications. Independent code review confirms all 5 ACs are met: VS Code model values correct (Opus for 1-2, Sonnet for 3-7), Claude Code cc_model values correct (same distribution), zero unresolved {{...}} template markers, standalone suite clean (22/22 personas up-to-date, exit 0).

Reviewed the full implementation surface (WP-001 YAML metadata + WP-002 build script changes) as context for this verification pass. The model resolution chain (persona.model !== undefined → sharedMeta.default_model || sharedMeta.cc_model || 'inherit') is logically correct and correctly guards with !== undefined rather than falsy check. Post-spread placement of computed model/cc_model in the context object prevents ...persona clobbering. ccModel correctly resolves as persona.cc_model ?? model (not the raw cc_model passthrough from sharedMeta), which is the right layering.
No blocking issues found. Implementation is minimal, idiomatic, and architecturally sound.

comments.note: WP-004 spec (Files Inspected table) lists pattern `personas/ledger/vs-code/*.agent.md` but actual build output is `personas/ledger/vs-code/*.md`. The `.agent.md` extension is applied during `sync-personas.js` deployment to `.vscode/`, not at build time. The spec documents the final deployed filename (matching `vs_file_name` in persona YAML) rather than the intermediate build artifact. Non-blocking — existing verifications are correct because they used actual file paths — but the WP spec text is mildly misleading for future readers.

The ccModel resolution (`persona.cc_model ?? model`) is a meaningful improvement over the prior pattern where cc_model was sourced directly from sharedMeta.cc_model. Under the new scheme, agents 1-2 that specify `model: 'Claude Opus 4.6'` will emit `model: 'Claude Opus 4.6'` in CC output as well (unless they add a per-persona cc_model override). This is the correct semantic: cc_model should reflect the resolved model. The chain is clean and self-documenting.

Carrying forward non-blocking observation from WP-002 review: scripts/build-personas.js ~L569 — the fallback chain `sharedMeta.default_model || sharedMeta.cc_model || 'inherit'` would benefit from a brief inline comment explaining why cc_model serves as a mid-level fallback (legacy configs that only have cc_model without default_model). Low-effort, high-yield for future maintainability.
